title: 2025 AMC 12B Problem 21
statement: Two non-congruent triangles have the same area. Each triangle has sides of length \(8\) and \(9,\) and the third side of each triangle has integer length. What is the sum of the lengths of the third sides?

solutions.text:
The area with included angle \(\theta\) is \(36\sin\theta,\) so two triangles of equal area use angles \(\theta\) and \(180^\circ - \theta,\) with cosines \(\pm\cos\theta.\) By the law of cosines the third sides satisfy \(t^2 = 145 \mp 144\cos\theta,\) hence \(t_1^2 + t_2^2 = 290.\) Since \(290\equiv2\pmod8,\) both integer sides must be odd. Checking the odd squares in the triangle-inequality range \(1\lt t\lt17\) leaves only \(11^2+13^2=121+169=290.\) Therefore the sum is \(24.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
